subject: Unexpected 429s due to quota aliasing — recovery plan and evidence
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novus.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected 429s impacting production (Novus)

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a flurry of 429 responses hitting our inference endpoints around 08:50 PT this morning. Error rate jumped to ~18% for a 6-minute window and then tapered, but it caused a small backlog in our worker pool and visible errors for customers.

Sample request IDs and timestamps are attached (request-samples.txt). We rolled a temporary retry backoff on our side, but this is causing increased latency for users. Can you confirm whether this was a routing, quota, or enforcement change on Redwood’s side?

We’re on plan "business-pro" and expected the committed capacity to cover this burst. Please advise next steps and whether you can (a) confirm root cause, (b) provide short-term mitigation to stop/rollback the enforcement, and (c) surface any compensation credits if this materially impacted customer SLA.

Thanks — apologies for the abrupt ping. I can jump on a call if helpful.

—
Sarah Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Novus AI
ops@novus.ai
[Attachment: request-samples.txt (text)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novus.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s impacting production (Novus)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the samples. We’re treating this as high priority. Quick summary of immediate actions we’re taking: 

- I’m opening an internal incident and assigning ops to collect enforcement logs and quota mappings.
- As an immediate mitigation, I’ve temporarily increased your tenant quota window and disabled the new enforcement rule for 30 minutes while we confirm the cause.
- We’ll gather logs and return a root-cause update within 90 minutes.

Can you confirm whether the traffic during the spike had an unusual pattern (e.g., many short-lived sessions, increased parallelism)? Any additional request IDs helps with correlation.

I’ll follow up with a full timeline and proposed remediation plan.

Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Preliminary root cause — quota aliasing during onboarding

Aditya / Rishi — forwarding preliminary findings from the runtime team. Please see the summary below and the attached quota_map.csv and patch.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Runtime Team <runtime@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Preliminary: aliasing between onboarding namespace and prod tenant bucket

Summary:
- During a recent onboarding job for a new tenant alias (internal ID alias-7f4), a misapplied mapping caused two tenant identifiers (novus-prod and alias-7f4) to reference the same quota bucket. When Novus experienced a burst, both identifiers consumed tokens from the same bucket, effectively halving the available concurrency for production.
- Enforcement rules applied at the bucket level, so the excess requests surfaced as 429s for legitimate Novus traffic.
- The mapping change was rolled out as part of a low-risk onboarding migration; the job’s validation step did not catch the duplicate bucket pointer because the mapping cache had an out-of-date index.

Immediate remediation performed:
1) We reverted the onboarding mapping (quota_map.csv) to point alias-7f4 to its own bucket.
2) Hotfix (quota_fix_patch.patch) applied to validation step to cross-check bucket ownership against the active index.
3) We temporarily increased Novus’s bucket tokens for the 30-minute window while we validated the fix.

Proposed next steps:
- Run a one-off scan across recent onboarding mappings to find other aliases pointing to shared buckets. (scheduled)
- Backfill evidence logs for Novus and deliver a compact evidence packet. (in progress)
- Provide a small service credit for the interruption and tighten onboarding guardrails.

[Attachments: quota_map.csv, quota_fix_patch.patch]

--- End forwarded message ---

Notes: runtime team marked this as a configuration race condition tied to cache staleness. Rishi, can you own the scan and evidence backfill? Aditya, recommend we send Novus a recovery plan and an evidence bundle, plus an upfront goodwill credit — say one week of committed capacity.

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: remediation-runbook.pdf (pdf)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novus.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s due to quota aliasing — recovery plan and evidence

Hi Sarah — quick update and next steps.

What happened (short): runtime onboarding created an alias that incorrectly referenced Novus’s quota bucket. When Novus spiked, the alias and your prod id competed for the same quota, causing excess 429s. This is a configuration aliasing issue during onboarding, not an enforcement algorithm bug.

What we did (immediate):
- Reverted the onboarding mapping and applied a validation hotfix to prevent alias-to-bucket collisions. (attachments: quota_map.csv, quota_fix_patch.patch)
- Temporarily expanded your bucket tokens during the incident window to limit customer impact.
- Collected and consolidated request-level evidence and request IDs (attached).

Planned follow-ups (we own these):
- Evidence packet: We’ll deliver a compact bundle with logs, timelines, and correlation IDs by EOD PT today.
- Account scan: Rishi will run a one-off scan to detect any other aliases that may share buckets and fix them if found. ETA: 48 hours.
- Post-incident remediation: We’ll add a guardrail to the onboarding pipeline and include a validation checkpoint in the change window.
- Compensation: As an initial goodwill gesture, we’ll credit one week of committed capacity to Novus’s account and are open to formal SLA crediting if your team requires it.

Action items for Novus:
- Confirm receipt of the evidence packet when you get it.
- If you want a joint walk-through, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning PT to review the logs and the patch.

I appreciate the quick report — this helped us detect the issue faster. Apologies for the disruption.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
